title: Strategy Sprint machine-readable output
description: The typed contract between a Strategy Sprint run and any program that consumes it. Each exercise writes a human markdown section AND a machine sidecar; this schema governs the sidecars and the run manifest that indexes them. ENVELOPE ONLY at this version: per-exercise payload shapes land additively under $defs/payloads and cannot break a consumer written against the envelope.
$comment: Version 0.1.0, 2026-08-05. Envelope is stable; payloads are not yet defined.

exerciseId.description: Stable identifier for a sprint step. Matches the skill directory name so the id, the slash command, and the sidecar filename never drift apart.

completionStatus.description: Operator-visible state of one step. Load-bearing: a missing sidecar alone is ambiguous between never-ran, ran-and-failed-to-write, and wrote-to-the-wrong-path, and those want different remediation. Recording status OUTSIDE the sidecar is what makes them separable.

manifest.description: Written to ${ARTIFACT_DIR}/output/sprint-manifest.yaml. THE ENTRY POINT: a consumer reads this first, then resolves sidecars from it. It exists because completion status cannot live only in the sidecar. A sidecar that is missing cannot tell you it was expected, so 'complete but absent' would be indistinguishable from 'never ran' and the three-way distinction would collapse back to two. The manifest is the thing that survives a sidecar that was never written.

sprintComplete.description: True only when every step with required=true has status 'complete'. Denormalized on purpose so a consumer can reject an unfinished run without walking the step list.

steps.description: One entry per sprint step, in execution order. Present for EVERY step including unrun ones: an absent entry means the manifest is stale, which is itself a defect worth raising rather than silently treating as unrun.

order.description: Execution position. Exercises 1-8 are the numbered sprint; companions (brand-voice) and prerequisites (tool-inventory) carry an order too so a consumer can sort one list.

required.description: False for optional steps. An optional step left unrun does not make the sprint incomplete.

sidecarPath.description: Path relative to ${ARTIFACT_DIR}, e.g. output/positioning.yaml. Recorded rather than derived so a consumer never has to reconstruct a filename convention, and so a step that legitimately writes somewhere else stays loadable.

failureReason.description: Set when status is 'failed'. Free text for a human; a consumer should surface it rather than parse it.

allOf.$comment: A failed step must say why. A status with no diagnosis pushes the investigation onto whoever finds it later, which is the expensive moment.
An unrun step has nothing to timestamp. Guarding this direction too, so a stale completedAt cannot survive a re-set to unrun.

sidecar.description: Written to ${ARTIFACT_DIR}/output/<exercise-id>.yaml by each exercise alongside its markdown section. Header is fixed; payload is open at this schema version.

sourceSection.description: The heading in marketing-strategy.md this sidecar mirrors, e.g. '## Channel Strategy'. Lets a consumer point a human at the prose behind a machine value.

confirmedByClient.description: Every exercise pauses for client confirmation before saving. False means drafted but not confirmed, a legitimate intermediate state that is NOT the same as complete. REQUIRED, not optional: a consumer that rejects unconfirmed content cannot treat an absent field as a safe default, because absent would be ambiguous between not-confirmed and exercise-never-recorded-it. That is the same ambiguity the manifest exists to break, one field over, so it is closed the same way: by making the producer state it.

payload.description: Exercise-specific content. OPEN at schema version 0.1.0: no properties are constrained yet. Per-exercise definitions land under $defs/payloads and are attached here by a future conditional block. Because this starts open and closes later, a consumer written against the envelope today keeps working: added payload constraints reject malformed NEW data, they do not change the envelope's shape.

allOf.$comment: Attach a payload schema once one exists for that exercise. An exercise with no definition yet keeps the open payload from 0.1.0, so adding definitions never breaks a consumer.

schemaVersion.description: Semver of THIS schema, not of the sprint. A consumer should reject a major it does not know rather than guess.

payloads.$comment: One definition per exercise, attached to sidecar.payload by the conditional in $defs/sidecar/allOf. Landing them additively is why the envelope shipped first. PATTERN, follow it for the remaining seven: derive fields from that exercise's own 'Step 3: Document' output block, keep every field OPTIONAL except the one or two the exercise exists to produce, and allow null with a stated reason rather than forcing a value the client did not give. A schema that forces completeness turns 'they would not tell us' into a fabricated number.

company-overview.description: Exercise 1. Mirrors the Company Snapshot, Key Metrics, Key Differentiators, Recent Momentum, Current Challenges and Competitive Landscape blocks.

pricing.description: Free text. Pricing structures do not reduce to a number and forcing one loses the structure.

productOverview.description: The 2-3 paragraph prose block, carried verbatim. Not decomposed: it is written for a human and any split would be this schema inventing structure the exercise never asked for.

metrics.description: Every metric is optional AND nullable. A client who will not share ARR is the normal case, and a schema that forces the field invites an estimate presented as a figure.

notProvided.description: Metric names the client declined or could not supply. EXPLICIT, because a null field alone cannot say whether it was asked. Same reason the run manifest exists.

differentiators.description: The exercise exists to produce these, so at least one is required.

evidence.description: The skill asks for evidence per differentiator. Nullable so an unevidenced claim is recorded AS unevidenced rather than dropped or invented.
